narrative: Today's ecology literature centres on fire recovery and climate-driven range dynamics: post-fire vegetation shifts in Siberian boreal forests are tracked via remote sensing, while a multispecies seed-addition experiment shows climate-driven range shifts lag at species' leading edges but not trailing ones. Behavioural and movement studies highlight how drought reshapes large carnivore space use and intensifies competitor avoidance, and ocean acidification is shown to constrain shoaling behaviour indirectly through habitat simplification rather than direct physiological stress. In trophic and symbiotic systems, a new superposition method streamlines food-web reconstruction from stable isotope data, and fungal guilds differ markedly in how climate versus dominant vegetation shapes their distributions. Invasion biology contributions include evidence that invasive crayfish reorganise entire environmental niche axes rather than simply shifting along them, and that selection has driven genome-size evolution in a globally invasive ragweed. On the conservation and methods front, a cross-continental zero-shot classifier extends frog-call recognition to previously unseen species, and a long-term dataset links poaching alleviation to mammal community recovery after an extreme ice-storm event. Grazing research shows goose herbivory restructures below-ground microbial function in sub-Arctic wetlands, while a review of the intermediate landscape complexity hypothesis finds mixed support for how local management versus landscape structure shapes insect biodiversity in farmland.
